patients.summary: Healthy young woman who works at an artisan bakery and is on a university student plan; joined in 2022 with functional constipation managed on psyllium. Two uncomplicated cystitis episodes in 2025, each treated with nitrofurantoin; otherwise routine preventive care.

documents.title: New Patient Intake Call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body:
Caller: patient (Sophia Roy, DOB 11/20/2000).

Wants to establish with the practice. Has been seen at her previous primary care office since childhood and would like to move closer to where she lives and works now. Mentioned she has a university student health plan as primary and her parents' PPO as secondary - both cards to be scanned at the visit.

Scheduled new patient physical 9/8 at 8:30. Membership agreement and intake forms sent to portal. Records release signed electronically; request faxed to prior office for immunizations and last visit notes.

No current concerns per pt.

documents.title: New Patient Visit - Establish Care
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT - ESTABLISHING CARE

21 y/o woman here to start with us. Grew up in the area, was followed at her previous primary care office until now. Works at an artisan bakery in town (early shifts) and is enrolled at the university, which is where her primary insurance comes from. Feels well. No acute concerns.

PMH: Constipation - functional, has had it for years. Goes a few days at a time without a BM when her schedule gets busy, otherwise fine. No blood, no weight loss, no night symptoms. Uses psyllium powder when she needs it, roughly a tablespoon in water, and that works for her. Never had a workup and never needed a prescription.
No other medical problems. No hospitalizations.
PSH: none.

Meds: psyllium powder PRN. No prescription meds. No supplements.
Allergies: NKDA.

FH: Mom has had a lot of bladder infections over the years. Dad has high blood pressure. Nobody with kidney disease or kidney stones that she knows of.

SH: Lives in Holyoke. Bakery associate, student. Never smoked. Alcohol socially on weekends, a drink or two. Denies drug use.

ROS: Negative except as above. Periods regular.

Exam:
Vitals as recorded. BMI normal.
Gen: well-appearing, pleasant.
HEENT: TMs clear, oropharynx without lesions. Neck supple, thyroid normal size, no lymphadenopathy.
CV: RRR, no murmur.
Lungs: CTA bilaterally.
Abd: soft, NT/ND, normal bowel sounds, no masses or HSM.
Ext: warm, no edema.
Skin: no rashes.
Neuro/psych: grossly nonfocal; mood and affect normal.

PHQ-2: 0. AUDIT-C: 2.

Assessment/Plan:
1. Health maintenance, new patient. Baseline CBC, CMP, lipids. HIV and hep C one-time screens offered and accepted. Tdap today - last one at 11 per her recollection, will confirm against outside records. Flu shot once supply is in, nurse visit next month. Cervical screening to start at her next physical.
2. Functional constipation - longstanding, no alarm features. TSH and calcium with today's labs. Keep using psyllium; talked about fluids and not putting off the bathroom on long shifts.

Return in 1 year for physical, sooner as needed. She has my cell for anything in between.

documents.author: front desk
documents.body:

- Last well visit there 2021: well, constipation noted, fiber suggested.
- Allergies on their list: NKDA.
- No screening labs or Pap on file.

Immunizations abstracted to chart. Tdap date matches what pt told us - the 9/8 Tdap is the 10-year booster.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
In after her bakery shift for flu and COVID booster. Screening questions negative; no prior vaccine reactions. VIS/EUA fact sheet given.

Influenza quadrivalent 0.5 mL IM left deltoid.
Pfizer bivalent booster 0.3 mL IM right deltoid.

Observed 15 min, tolerated well, left ambulatory.

documents.title: Constipation question
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi! Quick question, not urgent. We've had a lot of long shifts at the bakery lately and I basically don't get a real break, so I've been going like 3-4 days without going. The psyllium still works when I take it but I keep forgetting until it's already bad. Is it ok to just take it every day? Or should I be doing something else?

documents.title: RE: Constipation question
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Sophia - yes, taking the psyllium every day during the busy stretches is completely fine, and honestly works better that way than waiting until you're backed up. Same dose, lots of water with it. A water bottle at your station helps, and try to give yourself a few minutes in the morning before your shift, since that's when the gut is most active. If you start having pain, blood, or it stops responding to the fiber, let me know and we'll take a closer look.

documents.title: Annual Preventive Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual physical.

S: Doing well. Still at the bakery, more hours this summer. Constipation better since she started taking the psyllium daily on heavy weeks - most weeks now regular. No other concerns. Sexually active; reviewed STI screening, agreeable. LMP 2 weeks ago, regular.
Meds: psyllium PRN/daily on busy weeks. Allergies: NKDA.
SH: never smoker, a drink or two on weekends.

O: Vitals reviewed, normal.
General: well.
Neck: no thyromegaly or nodes.
Heart RRR without murmur; lungs clear.
Abdomen soft, nontender.
Pelvic: normal external genitalia; speculum exam with normal-appearing cervix, Pap collected. Tolerated with some nerves - first one, talked her through it.
Skin: no concerning lesions.

PHQ-2 0. AUDIT-C 2.

A/P:
- Health maintenance: first Pap today (age 22). Urine GC/CT. Tdap current (2022). Flu and COVID this fall, nurse visit.
- Functional constipation: stable on fiber.

RTC 1 year.

documents.title: Pap and STI screening results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Sophia, your Pap came back normal, and the chlamydia and gonorrhea tests were negative. With a normal Pap at your age the next one is in 3 years (2026). Thanks for getting through the first one!

Flu quadrivalent 0.5 mL IM L deltoid, lot recorded.
COVID (Pfizer, updated) 0.3 mL IM R deltoid, lot recorded.
Waited 15 min, no issues.
